# PR Review Checklist: Shared Package Definitions and Per-Request Terminology Settings

**Purpose**: Check the quality of the requirements (complete, clear, consistent, measurable) in spec 010 before
`/speckit-tasks` and during PR review. Focus: correctness and parity with 1.0.0, the API contract, security of
outbound calls, and memory and performance.
**Created**: 2026-11-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/http-api.md](../contracts/http-api.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Correctness and Parity: Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Does the spec state which terminology modes and which kinds of request the "identical to 1.0.0" requirement covers (only requests without `tx`/`txMode`, or also `server` and `ecosystem` contexts with a reachable server)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK002 - Does the spec define what happens to a package that has no recorded content hash: is it shared under `name#version` only, or never shared? (The plan says never shared; the spec is silent.) [Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK003 - Is "complete as shipped" defined precisely enough to decide, for a given definition, whether it is shared or private (for example, "has a snapshot in the package file")? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK004 - Are requirements stated for kinds of resource other than profiles (ValueSets, CodeSystems, SearchParameters) that the validation engine may also annotate while it runs, or does FR-020 cover only profiles? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK005 - Is a recovery requirement defined for the case where the differential check passes before release, but a result difference caused by sharing is found in production, given that sharing has no switch? [Gap, Recovery, Spec §FR-022]

## Correctness and Parity: Clarity and Consistency

- [x] CHK006 - Is "byte-identical after removing timing and request identifiers" specific about which OperationOutcome fields are removed or normalised, given that an OperationOutcome normally carries neither? [Clarity, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK007 - Is the source of the 1.0.0 expected results (a recorded baseline or a live 1.0.0 run) and the content of the corpus (which examples, how many invalid variants) specified well enough to repeat SC-004? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK008 - Is "fixed when the request starts" (FR-003) consistent with the per-call allowlist check (spec 007 FR-010c), which can still refuse a server partway through a request after an allowlist refresh? [Conflict, Spec §FR-003, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK009 - For mode `ecosystem`, is "drop the cached entries of the affected server only" defined, when one request may reach several servers chosen by routing? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the term for the cache identity used the same way in FR-012 ("effective setting (mode and server address)"), FR-013 ("affected server") and the Key Entities ("effective setting (mode and server)")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013, Key Entities]
- [x] CHK011 - Does the spec say whether code results cached during a request that used a `denied` default may be served to later requests, and for how long? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-012]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the order and precedence rule for duplicate canonical URLs (FR-021) stated in terms a tester can check, or only as "the same as today"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021]

## API Contract

- [x] CHK013 - Is the claim that every validate response reports the setting used (FR-010) consistent with the contract, which adds the `X-Tx-*` headers to 200 responses only? Is the header behaviour on 4xx and 503 answers specified? [Conflict, Spec §FR-010, Contract §3]
- [x] CHK014 - Is "`X-Tx-Server`: for `ecosystem` the default server, if any" clear about whether the registry's own default server counts, or only a server given in `tx` or the context setting? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK015 - Does FR-007 ("never echoes the address") agree with reusing `tx-server-not-registered`, whose existing detail text names the server? [Conflict, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK016 - Are empty values (`tx=`, `txMode=`) and parameters with surrounding spaces covered by the parsing rules? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-007]
- [x] CHK017 - Does the spec define the order of checks between the new 400/503 terminology errors and the existing `ig`, access (404/424), `profile` and `not-ready` errors? (At present it is only in the contract.) [Gap, Spec §FR-008, Contract §2]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the `Retry-After` behaviour of a request-level 503 `tx-registry-unavailable` specified (spec 007 defines it only for saved settings)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK019 - Is it specified what the usage record holds for the three new values when a request is refused before a setting is resolved, or by a terminology error? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK020 - Are the requirements for exposing the new headers to browsers (CORS) stated, given that FR-010 relies on callers being able to read them? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK021 - Are the context endpoint descriptions (include/PATCH answers and the "still applying" warning) covered by a requirement, now that a setting change no longer rebuilds? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the rule "requests without the new parameters MUST behave as in 1.0.0, apart from…" bounded by a list of every observable exception, such as cache hit rates and timing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027]
- [x] CHK023 - Does the Assumption "no database change is needed" agree with the requirement that the usage record carries three new values (which the plan stores through migration V16)? [Conflict, Assumptions, Spec §FR-010]

## Security and Outbound Calls

- [x] CHK024 - Does the spec require a bound on how often callers can make the service contact servers of their choosing (rate or count per key), or does it state that the per-request budget alone is enough? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK025 - Is it specified that the access checks (404/424) run before any terminology error, so that a caller cannot learn anything about a context it may not use? [Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK026 - Are logging requirements for the `tx` value (level, redaction) stated, consistent with the rule that the address is never echoed? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK027 - Is the edge case "the override is used when the context's own server was removed from the allowlist" consistent with FR-011's fail-closed rule, and is that intentional for a caller who names the removed server again? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK028 - Does "the code cache per server outcome" (FR-025) say whether a server address may appear in metric labels, given spec 007 FR-026's host-only rule? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK029 - Is "the validated resource MUST never be sent to the server" reconciled with spec 007 FR-014, which sends the package's value set and code system definitions with a request? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]

## Memory and Performance

- [x] CHK030 - Is "the memory held by the second context" defined with a measurement method (retained heap after a full collection, which classes, how the first context is excluded)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [x] CHK031 - Is the "per-context part" of the memory reservation (indexes, completed definitions, caches) quantified, or explicitly left to the plan with a stated way to measure it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024]
- [x] CHK032 - Is the memory budget of the one code cache (per-entry size × 50,000) stated in the requirements, so that FR-024 can be checked? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-024]
- [x] CHK033 - Is "estimated retained memory" for shared entries defined (how it is estimated and how accurate it must be)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK034 - Is "MUST NOT get slower" for definition lookups measurable (what is measured, which threshold), and is "reported in the plan" a requirement that a reviewer can verify? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK035 - Are the load profile, resource mix and environment of the SC-007 latency comparison specified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [x] CHK036 - Are the build-time conditions of SC-006 defined (cold or warm instance, packages already in the raw package cache or not)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK037 - Is the expected behaviour defined when memory is short and shared entries are only released once no context uses them (for example, a build refused although enough memory would be freed at the next garbage collection)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-019, §FR-024]
- [x] CHK038 - Is SC-008 ("releases that package's shared memory") measurable with a defined observation (metric value or heap figure) and time limit? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]

## Dependencies, Rollout and Assumptions

- [x] CHK039 - Are requirements defined for a rolling upgrade with mixed 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 instances, where a setting change rebuilds on the old instances but not on the new ones? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK040 - Is the assumption that definitions "complete as shipped" hold no context-dependent data backed by anything other than SC-004, or is it accepted as a risk in writing? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]
- [x] CHK041 - Is the change of the default value of `FV_TX_CACHE_SIZE` described as an upgrade-relevant change for operators who set it explicitly (its meaning changes from per context to per instance)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, §FR-028]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items CHK013, CHK015 and CHK023 point at likely contradictions between spec, contract and plan; resolve them first
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
